about: How each Short looks and sounds. plan.py gives every new Short one option per dimension: mostly the options that are keeping viewers watching (analytics/looks.json), sometimes the others, so the channel keeps learning and never looks templated. The weekly review adds new options and retires weak ones (set "retired": "<why>" rather than deleting, so old results still read).

punch.desc: bold capitals, white with a dark outline, the spoken word turns amber, 3 words at a time, lower middle
punch.retired: 2026-10-19: Charlie wants neat, minimal Shorts (no data yet: every look had 0 measured Shorts)

clean.desc: sentence case on a dark rounded panel, the spoken word in the accent colour, up to 4 words, lower third

pop.desc: one or two huge words at a time near the centre, the spoken word in the accent colour and slightly bigger
pop.retired: 2026-10-19: Charlie wants neat, minimal Shorts (no data yet: every look had 0 measured Shorts)

boxed.desc: bold capitals, the spoken word sits on an accent-coloured box, 3 words at a time
boxed.retired: 2026-10-19: Charlie wants neat, minimal Shorts (no data yet: every look had 0 measured Shorts)

minimal.desc: sentence case, white with a soft shadow and no outline or panel, the spoken word full white and the rest dimmed, up to 4 words, lower third
minimal.tested: TEST-W1019, 2026-10-19: clean and legible on dark and bright frames, YouTube and social layouts

low.desc: small sentence case (46px, about two thirds of the other styles), white with a soft shadow, no outline or panel, 3 words at a time, low in the frame (1385 to 1505 on YouTube, above its title rows), never over the middle of the picture

george_turbo.desc: British male, the george voice on Chatterbox-Turbo (350M, one-step decoder, no exaggeration or cfg), same pace

steady.desc: gentle zooms and pans, punch-ins only on impact beats

punchy.desc: bigger zooms, a punch-in at every new beat and harder hits
punchy.retired: 2026-10-19: Charlie wants neat, minimal Shorts (no data yet: every look had 0 measured Shorts)

calm.desc: slow drifts, the lightest punch-in only on the hook and payoff

grade.about: Colour grade on photos and footage (graphics and captions are not affected)

cinematic.desc: a little warmer and less saturated, darker edges

vivid.retired: 2026-10-19: Charlie wants neat, minimal Shorts (no data yet: every look had 0 measured Shorts)

opening.about: The first second, which decides whether people swipe away

graphic_first.desc: the hook's title or stat card is on screen from the first frame, over the subject

image_first.desc: the subject's picture alone for the first words, then the hook's card appears on the fourth word

style.about: How much text sits on the pictures and how fast they change (Charlie, 24 October: "fast changing images with minimal text", nothing covering the picture). A fixed test: 2 Shorts in 3 minimal, 1 in 3 standard (the control), until both arms have about 70 measured Shorts and drivers.csv (feature look_style) proves one better; then the winner takes 9 in 10 and the other keeps 1 in 10, so it stays measured. "assign" holds the split; looks.choose() uses it instead of the scores. Under minimal the opening dimension has no title card to reveal, so its arms differ only under standard.

minimal.desc: minimal text, fast pictures: the low captions; a name shows once, as a small corner tag for 1.2 seconds, never over a face or the middle; the category chip small and only in the first 2.5 seconds; title, stat, list, quote, date, timeline, versus and bar cards give way to the beat's full-screen photo (the numbers stay in the narration and the captions); a new picture every 1.2 to 1.8 seconds (more photos of the same subject, else the same photo with a new crop and move); a lighter shade over the picture

standard.desc: the look until 24 October, the control: captions from the captions dimension, a name label on every picture that has one, the category chip throughout, text cards for stats and lists, pictures as the board times them (a median of 4.3 seconds each)
